newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Hellenic issues warrants, rights.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Hellenic issues warrants, rights.

text.p: Cyprus's Hellenic Bank on Thursday announced a warrants and rights issue to boost its capital base after the takeover of Barclays Bank on- shore operations on the island earlier in the year.

"After the completion of the new issues the capital base of Hellenic Bank will exceed 60 million pounds ($130.2 million) which means it will have doubled to what it was two years ago," bank chairman Paschalis Paschalides told a news conference.
Last week the company announced an increase in its half- yearly pre-tax profit by 20.4 percent to 2.633 million pounds from 2.187 in the first half of 1995.

Hellenic will issue 6,434,579 rights shares with a nominal price of one pound at two pounds each, payable in three instalments from October 18 1996 to October 17 1997. Rights shares will be offered to existing shareholders at a ratio of one for every three shares held.

It will also issue 5,147,633 warrants, at 20 cents each, offered to shareholders at a ratio of one for every five ordinary shares held. The bank says it will raise 13.9 million pounds through the issue.
Hellenic, a Cypriot-owned bank, took over the on-shore operations of Barclays Bank PLC in April in a deal worth 8.5 million pounds.
"The purpose of the new issue is to further reinforce the capital base of the bank to better utilise the prospects arising through the purchase of Barclays on-shore operations," said Paschalides.
Hellenic enforced an early retirement scheme to terminate the services of 75 employees after the merger at a cost of two million pounds in July, Paschalides said.
The bank has 120 branches and employs 1,150 people.
